result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers spot the Free/Starter overlap, the fake 'limited time' discount and the Agency crawl-volume mismatch. Neither says outright that site and user counts, not pages, are doing the gating. B is slightly better: it deals with the mid-tier gap more fully, explains the legal risk of the fake discount, and gives a concrete revised price ladder to test. A does more to say what already works (Team fits freelancers, Free's limits are reasonable) and is clearer about its assumptions. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers flag the false 'limited time' label, the overly deep 55% annual discount, the Team-to-Agency gap and the 480x crawl-volume mismatch. B is somewhat better. It ties price to cost per 1,000 checks, explicitly calls Free and Starter nearly identical, and notes what already works (Starter for single-site owners, a reasonable Free limit). It also lists its assumptions and what would change its advice. A gives a useful full tier sketch with a priced middle tier, but it barely says what already works.
